script: German soldiers wore spiked helmets that protected nothing at all. In 1843, the Prussian military introduced the Pickelhaube, a leather helmet topped with a sharp metal spike. Officials claimed the spike could deflect a sword blow aimed at the head. But the real reason ran deeper: the spike made soldiers look taller, fiercer, more intimidating on a battlefield full of cameras and journalists. It did nothing against bullets, and nothing against shrapnel. When the First World War began, soldiers wore these helmets into real combat, and died in numbers that proved the point instantly. Within months, the military quietly pulled the spiked helmets from the front lines, replacing them with plain steel. They had known the spike was decoration long before the war ever proved it. German soldiers wore spiked helmets that protected nothing, and the military let them believe otherwise.

description:
